newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - South Korean newspapers - July 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Korean newspapers - July 10.

text.p: The following is a summary of major stories in leading South Korean newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy.
- Korea lodged a strong protest to Japan over its repeated seizure of Korean fishing boats and warned of possible negative impacts the siezure could have on bilateral relations.
- North Korean defector Hwang Jang-yop holds a news conference at the headquarters of the Agency for National Security Planning in Seoul.
- Kang In-sop, senior presidential secretary for political affairs, resigned over a controversial remark regarding the ruling New Korea Party's race for its presidential candidate.
- Samsung Group on Wednesday launched its think tank to develop a business strategy for the 21st century.
- North Korea recorded a negative 3.7 percent rate of growth in its real gross national product last year, the Bank of Korea said on Wednesday.
- Hunger-stricken North Korea announced on Wednesday that it was abandoning the world calendar and introducing its own based on the birth of its founding Stalinist leader Kim Il-sung.
- Construction of the high-speed railway linking Seoul and Pusan is now scheduled to be completed in 2006, four years behind the original deadline.
